title: Sessile Oak: Ancient Sessile Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: The pedunculate oak's rarer, straighter-trunked cousin. Meet Pfaueninsel's door-pierced sessile oaks and a Groningen survivor saved from the saw.
intro: Sessile oak, Quercus petraea, is the pedunculate oak's straighter-trunked cousin: its acorns sit directly on the twig with no stalk, while its leaves carry the longer stalk the other species' acorns lack. In the Netherlands it is a genuine rarity, over 95 percent of the country's oaks are pedunculate, which is what made a single tree in Groningen's Zuiderplantsoen worth a public campaign when the city nearly felled it for a footpath in 2025. Germany's royal gardens kept better company: on Pfaueninsel, the private island a Prussian king filled with peacocks and follies, sessile oaks were already a century old when the landscaping began in 1793, and three still stand there, one carrying a door cut clean through its trunk since some forgotten fit of eighteenth century theatre. These are the sessile oaks mapped on the site so far.
